desc:
A tape is built by reading the string s from left to right, starting with an empty tape:

  • a lowercase letter is appended to the end of the tape;
  • a digit d (from 2 to 9) makes the tape repeat: the whole tape written so far is replaced by d copies of itself placed one after another.

The final tape can be astronomically long (it can have more than 1018 letters or much more), so you cannot build it. Given a 1-indexed position k, return the letter at position k of the final tape, as a one-character string.

Example: for s = 'leet2code3' the tape is 'leet', then 'leetleet', then 'leetleetcode', then three copies of that (36 letters). Position 10 is 'o'.
constraints: s consists of lowercase letters and digits 2 to 9, and starts with a letter
1 ≤ k ≤ 10<sup>9</sup>, and k is at most the length of the final tape
hints: Compute the length of the tape after each character. Letters add one, digits multiply. Stop as soon as the length reaches k: later characters cannot change what is at position k.
A digit d turns tape T into T repeated d times, so position k in the new tape holds the same letter as position k mod len(T) in T.

Walk backwards from the stopping point with the current length: for a digit, divide the length by d and set k = k % length; for a letter, if k % length == 0 this letter is the answer, otherwise reduce the length by one.
editorial: First find the shortest prefix of s whose tape is at least k letters long. Later characters only append after position k or repeat the tape, and repeating never changes any earlier position, so the answer comes from this prefix. Its length stays below roughly 9 * 109, so there are no overflow worries.

Now undo the prefix from the end with a running length size. Before handling a character, reduce k %= size. If the character is a letter: when k == 0 (k pointed at the last letter of the tape) this letter is the answer; otherwise decrease size by one. If the character is a digit: the tape was d copies of the previous tape, so size //= d; the reduction of k already mapped it into the first copy. Each character is processed twice, so the time is O(n) with O(1) extra space. It is a stack-like undo of the character stream.
